title: Hardship assessment summary, case 2026/0412
body: The applicant reports weekly earnings of $820, based on payslips from June to August 2026. A delegate may waive the debt where recovery would cause severe financial hardship [1]. The applicant has no other source of income. The applicant lives alone. Weekly rent of $380 leaves limited capacity to repay the $4,860 debt. Research on discretion in overpayment recovery supports a case-by-case approach [2] [3]. Most hardship waivers are decided within 28 days [4].
references:
References
[1] Social Security Act 1991 (Cth) s 1237AAD.
[2] Spicker, P. (2023). Discretion in overpayment recovery. Journal of Social Welfare and Family Law.
[3] Edmiston, D. (2022). Indentured: benefit deductions, debt recovery and welfare disciplining. Journal of Social Policy, 51(3).
[4] Henderson, J. (2019). Hardship waivers and decision timeframes. Australian Journal of Administrative Law, 26(3).

title: Eligibility review note, case 2026/0587
body: Identity was verified against the identity verification record on 3 September 2026. The applicant has been a permanent resident since 2019. Declared fortnightly income is $1,240. A medical certificate covers 1 September 2026 to 28 February 2027.

title: Briefing: hardship waiver trends
body: Under the current policy, a delegate may waive a debt where recovery would cause serious financial hardship [1]. Decisions should be made within 21 days of a complete application. A 2021 national study found that 62 per cent of waiver applications are approved on first assessment [2]. Comparable schemes report approval rates above 70 per cent [3]. Delegates must record the basis of each decision [4].
references:
References
[1] Social Security Act 1991 (Cth) s 1237AAD.
[2] Okafor, L. & Brennan, S. (2021). First-assessment outcomes in debt waiver schemes: a national study. Australian Journal of Public Administration, 80(2).
[3] Edmiston, D. (2024). Indentured: Benefit deductions, debt recovery and welfare disciplining. Social Policy & Administration.
[4] Marsh, K. (2020). Recording administrative decisions. Administrative Review Quarterly, 12(1).

title: Case note drafted by the case update agent, case 2026/0412
body: The applicant applied for waiver of debt on the grounds of financial hardship. The applicant confirmed employment at Example Logistics continues. A letter advising the applicant of a possible overpayment was sent and no response was received. The debt of $4,860 was raised on 20 August 2026. The applicant has since resigned from Example Logistics.
